messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: Re: expanding reactiveValues
parts:
here's what I want to do - have a set of reactiveValues with a set of values.

queries = reactiveValues()
fetchers = reactiveValues()

when I add or update a query in queries, I have some observers which create or replace a fetcher in fetchers.

When a fetcher completes (my asynchronous URL work) the completed field of the member of fetchers is set, and the observer for that pulls the finished value and generates an output.

At the moment, the set of actors are discrete functions.

To register a new query/actor path, you could do this:

observer({ if(controlReactives$appStarted) queries$mylovelyquery = "SELECT FUN FROM STUFF" })

renderPlot({ if(fetchers$mylovelquery$complete) plot(fetchers$mylovelyquery$data) })

The internals would handle the rest. 

-Alex

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: expanding reactiveValues
parts:
Hi Alex -

Here's a demonstration of the dependencies taken with names():

# Create a reactive values object
v <- reactiveValues(a=1, b=2)

# Add an observer that takes a dependency on v's names, and prints them
# when invalidated (and invalidated objects are flushed)
observe({
  print(names(v))
})

# Flush invalidated objects: prints names(v)
shiny:::flushReact()
# [1] "a" "b"

# No effect on second run; observer wasn't invalidated
shiny:::flushReact()
# <No output>

# Change value of a: observer isn't invalidated
v$a <- 2
shiny:::flushReact()
# <No output>

# Add a new object; observer is invalidated
v$c <- 3
shiny:::flushReact()
# [1] "a" "b" "c"

-Winston

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: expanding reactiveValues
parts:
Exactly, and that's how the unit tests for Shiny are done:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/inst/tests/test-reactivity.r

For asking the state of reactive objects, there's a function called execCount(), which will tell you how many times a reactive expression or observer has run.

To get other information, in the Shiny tests we have the reactives set values in the parent environment with the <<- operator.

-Winston
